levels.note: background blockMesh divisions scaled up from production (46x40x67 vs 41x36x60); every other setting (surface levels (3 4), eMesh level 3, kOmegaSST, 300 iterations, velocity 100) identical to production.

background blockMesh divisions scaled up again (51x45x75); same recipe as fine-uq/production. Added specifically to get a second successive triple within the valid same-recipe family, per uq-b52-ladder-monotonicity lesson update.

numerical.method: successive Cd increments GROW with refinement instead of shrinking; ladder not in the asymptotic range, conservative band, largest spread times 1.25

recipe_audit.finding: coarse and medium rungs used nearBody refinement-shell level 1 (max overall cell level 3); intermediate, production, fine-uq, and finer2 used nearBody level 2 (max overall cell level 4). Confirmed both from log.snappyHexMesh ('Refinement level N for all cells inside nearBody' and the 'Cells per refinement level' histograms) and from sdk/scripts/run_uq_studies.py's own documented castellated-level floor/degenerate-ladder issue. Only {intermediate, production, fine-uq, finer2} share one refinement recipe (background-mesh density is the only thing that varies); coarse and medium are not extrapolation-comparable to the other four and should not be mixed into a single Richardson/GCI fit with them.

iterative_audit.question: whether the valid family's GROWING Cd increments are a discretization property or an artifact of a fixed 300-iteration budget spent on progressively larger meshes
iterative_audit.method: force history read directly from each rung's own postProcessing/forceCoeffs1/0/coefficient.dat; window means and 2-sigma over the final 60 iterations, plus the drift between the 150-225 and 225-300 windows
iterative_audit.finding: Iterative error is ruled out. Neither finest rung prints OpenFOAM's 'SIMPLE solution converged' message, so convergence was measured from the force history rather than assumed: both are stationary to a final-window 2-sigma of 1.07e-05 (fine-uq) and 2.25e-06 (finer2), with halves-drift below 1e-06. The finer rung is the MORE settled of the two, not the less. Those figures are two to three orders of magnitude below the 2.702e-03 grid increment they would have to explain. The increments grow because the discretization does, and the ladder is diverging for a reason more iterations cannot reach.
